notes.note: The round-2 fix for ـًا now reads '-an (ending: an indefinite object; also adverbs like shukran)'. In this lesson ـًا marks the predicate of لَيْسَ, not an object. It matches the course's 'object form' wording, so it is not wrong, but '-an (the ending after laysa/kāna, on objects and on adverbs like shukran)' would fit the lesson better.
مَنْ فِي الْبَيْت؟ is 'Who is in the house?' / 'Who is at home?'; the English 'Who lives in the house?' is a free rendering. Acceptable in context.

The Arabic field contains the English '(to Daniel)', so the transliteration starts with a lower-case 'hal akalti samakan? (to Daniel)'. Moving '(to Daniel)' into the why text would keep the Arabic field clean.
Layla is Lebanese and the trip is to Beirut; in Lebanon July is normally تَمُّوز. يُولْيُو is correct MSA (Egyptian/Maghrebi usage), so this is only a register/culture note.

الْمُبَارَاة in pause prints 'al-mubārāh' (ALA-LC -āh for tāʾ marbūṭa after alif), while elsewhere tāʾ marbūṭa is silent ('sayyāra'). It follows ALA-LC, so not an error, but learners may wonder about the -h.

summary: I read all 2,775 lines of audit/days-31-40.txt (days 31–40): about 535 Arabic strings with their transliterations, ~1,990 seg glosses and 722 tap glosses (330 tap lines), plus every translation, literal, mistake card, grammar note and quiz key, checking the syntax of each sentence before judging case endings and opening the round-2 merged report to avoid re-reporting fixed items. The Arabic itself is clean: laysa/lastu/laysat + accusative, kāna/kānat + accusative (incl. kunnā ʿasharata), number–counted-noun agreement (ʿashru sanawātin, ʿishrūna sanatan, thalāthatu akhwāl, ʿasharatu aḥfād), hollow-verb past (zurnā, zurtumā, nimtu), mā + past negation, qabla/baʿda (an) + noun/verb, idāfa family chains, abāhu/abāka object forms, dual forms (yadayya, naẓīfatāni, faʿaltumā) and the round-2 fixes (ṭawīl gloss, kānū gloss, the day 40 fill-the-gap options, the qāf description) are all correct. I found 0 Arabic, agreement, verb, translation or answer-key errors. Errors: 5, all minor: 1 gloss (مُنْذُ tapped as 'since, for' in 6 taps of the day-38 lesson that teaches it as 'ago'; 6 of 722 taps wrong) and 4 engine problems in the ⟶ lines (wa-Lisāmī; unhyphenated wa-/fa- clitics in 5 lines; bare ة/ْ/أ with empty transliteration, ة being a regression; Chicago and Karim not capitalised). 5 notes.
